scope: Proposition 5.1 (Exterior orthogonality) of the manuscript “The joint scaling limit of critical Ashkin-Teller currents” (preprints/The-joint-scaling-limit-of-critical-Ashkin-Teller-currents-October-6-2026/main.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 233 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 cec129cca8c2a0a6), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 40. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: Let Q be a square and let B be a concentric disk whose radius is less than one thousandth of the side length of Q. For ϕ ∈ C∞ c (B), let Eδ(Q) be the sigma-field generated by the full pair of spins outside Q, the W states on mutually dual edge pairs whose incident corner-grid plaquette is disjoint from Q (and hence the corresponding N states), and all height increments computable there. Then ∥EPδ [Xδ | Eδ(Q)]∥1 −→ 0. (5.2) The same assertion holds under any sequence of flat-domain laws having a fixed larger square Q+ compactly in their interiors, with Q ⊂ Q+. It is uniform over those domains, including the component laws supplied by an earlier exact flat cut. In the latter case it is applied to the conditional law at that cut, before any later data are revealed. Additive height constants do not affect the assertion.
